title: System Design — Estimation and interview framework

questions.question: Back-of-the-envelope estimation is meant to:
options: Produce exact production capacity plans down to the last disk platter in real production systems at scale.
Use thought experiments and common numbers to feel which designs can meet requirements.
Replace load testing forever so you never measure a real system in real production systems at scale.
Prove that every design needs exactly 64 servers and no other count in real production systems at scale.
questions.explanation: estimates you create using a combination of thought experiments and common performance numbers

reference.book: System Design Interview – An Insider's Guide
reference.excerpt: estimates you create using a combination of thought experiments and common performance numbers

questions.question: From typical latency intuition Xu highlights:
options: Disk seeks are faster than memory access in almost every case in real production systems at scale.
Memory is fast but disk is slow — avoid unnecessary disk seeks when possible.
Cross-datacenter network hops are free and should be ignored in real production systems at scale.
Compression is always slower than sending raw terabytes over the internet.
questions.explanation: Memory is fast but the disk is slow. Avoid disk seeks if possible

reference.book: System Design Interview – An Insider's Guide
reference.excerpt: Memory is fast but the disk is slow. Avoid disk seeks if possible

questions.question: In Xu’s Twitter-style QPS exercise, the first move is to:
options: Buy GPUs before clarifying monthly active users or posts per day.
State assumptions (MAU, daily usage, posts/day) then derive DAU and QPS.
Assume zero reads because only writes matter for capacity in real production systems at scale.
Skip units so 5 might mean 5 bytes or 5 petabytes interchangeably.
questions.explanation: Assumptions: • 300 million monthly active users… Estimations: Query per second (QPS)

reference.book: System Design Interview – An Insider's Guide
reference.excerpt: Assumptions: • 300 million monthly active users… Estimations: Query per second (QPS)

questions.question: Step 1 of Xu’s interview framework emphasizes:
options: Answering instantly like Jimmy without clarifying requirements in real production systems at scale.
Slowing down to ask questions, clarify requirements, and state assumptions.
Drawing microservices before you know what the product does in real production systems at scale.
Refusing to discuss scale until after coding every endpoint in real production systems at scale.
questions.explanation: DON’T be like Jimmy… Slow down. Think deeply and ask questions to clarify requirements

reference.book: System Design Interview – An Insider's Guide
reference.excerpt: DON’T be like Jimmy… Slow down. Think deeply and ask questions to clarify requirements

questions.question: Over-engineering in interviews is a red flag because:
options: Interviewers only want the most complex possible topology every time.
Engineers chase design purity and ignore trade-offs and compounding costs.
Simple designs are illegal in all FAANG interview rubrics in real production systems at scale.
Trade-offs only exist after the company has a billion users in real production systems at scale.
questions.explanation: Over-engineering is a real disease… ignore tradeoffs

reference.book: System Design Interview – An Insider's Guide
reference.excerpt: Over-engineering is a real disease… ignore tradeoffs

questions.question: True or false: Xu says there is no perfect answer; the interview simulates collaborative problem solving on an ambiguous problem.
questions.explanation: The problem is open-ended, and there is no perfect answer

reference.book: System Design Interview – An Insider's Guide
reference.excerpt: The problem is open-ended, and there is no perfect answer

questions.question: When doing estimation math in an interview, Xu advises:
options: Spend minutes computing 99987 / 9.1 exactly with long division.
Round and approximate; write assumptions; label units clearly.
Never say QPS out loud because interviewers dislike numbers.
Hide all assumptions so the interviewer cannot challenge them.
questions.explanation: Rounding and Approximation… Write down your assumptions… Label your units

reference.book: System Design Interview – An Insider's Guide
reference.excerpt: Rounding and Approximation… Write down your assumptions… Label your units
